policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads plural 'the inhabitants of Beth-shean', matching the plural qere ישבי, but an English plural does not exclude the ketiv ישב: the singular participle יושב is a collective regularly rendered 'inhabitants' in the ASV, and the same verse's other clauses ('the inhabitants of Dor', 'of Ibleam', 'of Megiddo') carry no distinguishing wording either. The only note on the verse is a hebrew_gloss on 'towns' (Hebrew daughters), which is unrelated to this lemma; no textual_variant note is mapped here. Base fallback (qere) carries the projection.
